EMET 100: EMET 100 is a first semester course intended to introduce first-year EMET students to a core set of computational tools and simulation software that will be used repeatedly throughout the EMET curriculum to investigate engineering/technical problems.
EMET 215: EMET 215 is intended to introduce the student, in both a lecture and site visit setting, to production planning, and production routing for the purpose of part creation and assembly, manufacturing process and equipment layout required for an assembly of artifacts from raw materials to shipping, including material handling.
EMET 222: The purpose of this course is to give students the ability to calculate engineering stresses, strains, and deflections in members subjected to different types of loading using the applied forces and reactions obtained from static equilibrium calculations.
EMET 225: This course is designed to provide engineering technology students with knowledge in solving problems using fundamental laws and equations of motion that are applied to particles and rigid bodies.
EMET 230: Introduction to concepts of structured programming, data acquisition, computerized interfaces, and graphical user interfaces.
EMET 325: Study of operation, application and specification of AC/DC electrical drive motors, servos, actuators, control units and power converters.
EMET 326: Transmission of force and motion using linkages, cams, gears, belts, and hydraulic and pneumatic drives.
EMET 330: Fundamentals of measuring, transmitting, and recording temperature, pressure, flow, force, displacement, and velocity; laboratory component emphasizes systems used in manufacturing.
EMET 350: Fundamentals of quality including statistics, probability, and design of experiments.
EMET 351: The objective of Quality Control, Inspection, and Design is to introduce the student to fundamentals of quality including statistics, probability, and process control.
EMET 394: Students collaborate on research and design of appropriate solutions to real-life problems and projects.
EMET 395: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
EMET 396: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
EMET 397: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
EMET 402: Overview of the topics covered on the Fundamentals of Engineering Exam administered by the NCEES for the purpose of earning a Professional Engineering license.
EMET 403: This course involves the planning and preliminary design activities for the capstone electro-mechanical design project.
EMET 405: Introduction to the principles of fluid mechanics and heat transfer with emphasis on the application to practical problems.
EMET 410: Introduction to analog feedback control theory and computer simulation and analysis using Matlab; laboratory study of feedback systems.
EMET 430: A second course in PLCs covering sequencing/shift instructions, program flow control, data and math instructions, PID loops, and machine communication.
EMET 433: Exploration of central concepts and technologies of smart manufacturing with focus on the internet of things, data analytics for production data, simulation and digital twins, and process and manufacturing systems optimization.
EMET 440: Planning, development, and implementation of electro-mechanical design project; includes formal report writing, project documentation, group presentations, project demonstrations.
EMET 441: Planning and development activities for the capstone electro-mechanical design project.
EMET 442: Assembly and testing activities for the electro-mechanical design project.
EMET 495: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
EMET 496: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
EMET 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
